modality_independent_principles: Match information emphasis to user risk, consequence, and decision context.

Make personalization inspectable and controllable by naming the signal or basis, separating recommendations from recent and saved content, and retaining direct search, category, history, notification, and library controls.

Offer retention alternatives only when they genuinely map to a user need and disclose their effect on charges, access, holdings, orders, progress, and future cancellation; keep cancellation visible and independently available.

Name audience reach in concrete terms and explain moderation or participation consequences, distinguishing who can view, who can comment, who can reuse, where copies are saved, and where content is distributed.

Structure B2B onboarding around the operating model and accountable outcomes: separate identity, data connection, workspace structure, security, billing, member invitation, customization, and the first assigned or completed unit of real work.

Make administrative scope explicit across organization, workspace, product, team, and individual levels, showing effective policy, role, authentication, member or seat population, entitlement, save state, and audit history together.

Represent assignment, discussion, state change, dependency, approval, notification, subscription, and completion as different mechanisms with accountable actors and lifecycle; activity alone must not imply ownership or completion.
Explain regulated data requests in plain language by naming what is collected, why it is necessary, and what the user will do next.
Keep clinical measurements self-describing through name, value, unit, reference range, time, trend, source, and interpretation, separating educational context from individualized medical advice.
Separate patient-reported behavior, observed symptoms, clinician-authored findings, automated interpretation, and completed-care claims so one evidence class cannot silently stand in for another.
Treat consent as an inspectable agreement tied to the service, disclosure, signer, date, modality, data use, and withdrawal or support path rather than as an unexplained checkbox.
Support comparison through aligned decision fields, stable units, definition help, variant equivalence, and visible differences rather than forcing memory across product pages.
Make the checkout total reconstructable from items, quantities, discounts, delivery, service charges, regulatory fees, tax, tip, deposits, subscriptions, and temporary authorization.
Treat fulfillment and return as explicit lifecycles with current stage, next expected event, deadline, affected item, amount, payment destination, tracking, support, and safe cancellation.
Distinguish followed, searched, saved, editorial, sponsored, trending, and recommended content, exposing enough source and rationale for users to understand why an item entered the feed.
Name publication reach and participation consequences concretely so viewers, commenters, reusers, community members, and external destinations are not collapsed into one public state.

Make creator economics reconstructable through audience source, active and paid members, trials, conversions, cancellations, tier changes, revenue, payout state, and the content or offer that produced each result.
At booking review, preserve the exact itinerary, traveler identity, operator, segment, baggage, ticket relationship, amendability, refundability, fees, add-ons, payment, currency, and final total.

Treat delay, cancellation, schedule change, missed connection, and supplier cancellation as distinct states with source, last update, affected segment, time consequence, and accountable recovery party.
Build trip continuity around a time-zone-aware sequence of transport, lodging, activities, check-in, documents, local details, and support rather than a disconnected reservation archive.
Separate effort, continuity, mastery, completion, assessment, and credential state so time spent or streak length cannot stand in for learning outcome.

At enrollment, preserve program outcome, format, instructor or authority, start and end timing, cadence, prerequisites, capacity or learner scope, price, discounts, tax, cancellation, and total commitment.

Make instructional analytics actionable by connecting aggregate completion or score to individual learners, assignment state, last activity, due state, evidence, and a proportionate intervention route.
Make observability reconstructable from environment, version, time window, request or trace identity, model or service, latency, cost, usage, errors, tool calls, feedback, and raw drilldown.
Treat prompts and agent configuration as versioned artifacts binding model, instructions, variables, tools, parameters, datasets, evaluators, sharing scope, and deployment state.
Before agent or automation rollout, expose audience, trigger, tools, data scope, permissions, unresolved-case behavior, expected affected population, human review, go-live state, and rollback route.
Lead with a distinctive, decision-relevant point of view and immediately clarify the audience, business situation, or transformation it applies to; do not ask a slogan to carry the full proposition.
Describe each capability through the business change, mechanism, and boundary it addresses rather than presenting an undifferentiated inventory of consulting deliverables.
Treat thought leadership as inspectable intellectual evidence: identify the question or audience, format, date, author or expert, evidence basis, and a concise reason the finding matters now.
Structure client impact around the client context, challenge, intervention, and resulting outcome, attaching metrics to timeframe and comparison basis instead of relying on logos or isolated numbers.

Keep point of view, capability architecture, client proof, intellectual property, expert profiles, and engagement language mutually reinforcing so the corporate story does not fragment into unrelated content systems.

applicability: all supported sections and multi-step flows
modality_independent_principles: Sequence information around orientation, decision, consequence, and recovery.
Establish relevance by naming the audience or situation and the concrete outcome before introducing supporting detail.
Sequence evidence according to the claim and decision risk, using adoption proof, quantitative support, process detail, or safeguards where each is relevant.
Preserve the promised outcome and included value at the point where the user chooses a plan, trial, signup, or upgrade.
State the full commitment model before the action, including price basis, cadence, immediate charge, trial transition, renewal, and material tax or cancellation conditions.
Explain the immediate benefit or necessity before requesting personal data, permissions, or effort.
Present the full cost as a reconstructable equation that updates when taxes, fees, discounts, tips, add-ons, quantities, or fulfillment choices change.
Carry material fulfillment, eligibility, cancellation, and refund consequences into final review instead of leaving them only at discovery.

Organize the dashboard around current state, unresolved consequence, and the next meaningful decision, placing urgent eligibility, incident, risk, overdue, or failed-work signals above descriptive totals and secondary exploration.
Attach each headline measure to its comparison basis, target, denominator, composition, or trend so the value communicates direction and significance rather than a context-free snapshot.
Distinguish healthy zero, empty result, missing data, stale data, excluded scope, not configured, and no recent activity; each state should explain what is known and the most useful next step.

Keep the active query, category, location, date, audience, and other material scope visible beside the results, representing applied constraints as removable state so users can explain, narrow, or broaden the set without reconstructing the search.

Expose the attributes that determine choice at result level, including price basis, availability, eligibility, source, recency, location, scope, or commitment cost, and align comparable fields so users do not have to open every item to judge fit.

Separate retrieval modes such as recent, saved, popular, editorially curated, sponsored, personalized, and query-matched results, and disclose the rationale closely enough that familiarity, payment, or recommendation does not masquerade as relevance.

applicability: draft, review, publish, activate, and export flows
modality_independent_principles: Keep artifact identity, editable draft state, save or sync status, and consequential release state visibly distinct, using a review boundary before publish, activate, send, share broadly, deploy, or export.
Attach validation to the exact field, node, step, asset, audience, or output setting that blocks progress, explain the consequence, and provide a direct route to repair before the release action.

At release, summarize output scope, audience or access, timing, quality, destination, ownership, restrictions, and irreversible or costly consequences, then show progress and a recoverable result state.

Keep collaboration anchored to the exact artifact, object, passage, task, message, source evidence, or version under discussion, preserving author, time, location, and current state so feedback cannot drift from its subject.

Represent discussion, assignment, state transition, decision, approval, and permission as distinct record types with their own owners and lifecycle; a comment, reaction, or personal done state must not imply team completion or authorization.

Make handoffs explicit through one accountable owner, required outcome, due or review condition, dependency and source context, notification scope, and acceptance state, retaining the conversation as evidence rather than as the task itself.

Identify the setting's subject and scope before the control, distinguishing personal, workspace, organization, product, environment, audience, and inherited policy so users know who and what will change.

Explain the operational consequence beside each material control, including visibility audience, notification event and channel, billing commitment, authentication reach, integration data flow, or accessibility behavior.

Separate reversible preference changes from consequential security, privacy, ownership, billing, publication, and deletion actions, using stronger review, authorization, and confirmation in proportion to impact.
Name the requester, granting identity, resource owner, and destination before asking for access, distinguishing a person, application, service, group, administrator, and external party.

Describe permissions as concrete data reads, writes, actions, exports, downloads, comments, edits, administration, billing, or impersonation capabilities, separating independently optional scopes to support least privilege.
State duration and lifecycle explicitly through one-time, while-in-use, ongoing, pending, expiring, deactivated, or revoked status, and provide the later review and revocation path at grant time.

applicability: uploads, imports, synchronization, and background jobs
modality_independent_principles: Classify the state before designing it: distinguish first use, healthy zero activity, zero results under a query or filter, unavailable data, access restriction, validation failure, transient failure, and partial completion so the explanation and recovery match the actual condition.
State what happened, which object or step is affected, and the known cause in operational language; when the cause is unknown, say what is known without replacing uncertainty with a generic message.

For consequential retries, disclose whether the prior action completed, failed before commitment, may still be pending, or affected only a subset; prevent ambiguous repeated submissions and preserve a receipt or diagnostic reference when outcome is uncertain.

Model the corporate website as a multi-audience information system: identify the primary business audience, then provide explicit routes for customers, partners, investors, media, candidates, communities, and existing users without giving every audience equal top-level weight.

Keep a stable institutional hierarchy across header, homepage, footer, search, and subsites, using the same language for products or capabilities, solutions, industries, resources, company, and audience-specific destinations.

Make newsroom, sustainability, governance, and impact content inspectable through date, reporting period, category, metric definition, accountable contact, archive continuity, and a route to the underlying report or release.
Use a consistent expressive hierarchy without allowing style to hide meaning.

Establish an explicit editorial hierarchy with one lead idea or story, a bounded supporting set, and a separate route into the broader archive; do not make every item compete at the same visual level.

Treat headline, deck, category or format, author or publisher, date, and reading scope as one orientation system, keeping the metadata close enough to the story that it cannot be mistaken for another item.
Vary card size or composition only when it communicates a real difference in priority, format, or reading path; preserve a stable content grammar for comparable items.

Create premium expression through selective emphasis: establish one focal product, promise, or experience, then preserve visible orientation, evidence, and action rather than equating scarcity of information with exclusivity.

Turn material and craft into inspectable evidence by connecting close imagery to process, provenance, finish variation, durability, technical specification, compatibility, or the qualities the buyer will receive.

Keep price, duration, billing cadence, included benefits, eligibility, fulfillment, cancellation, and material limitations legible at the commitment boundary; premium presentation must not make the transaction less inspectable.
Create calm through controlled attention by establishing one dominant status, decision, or starting action before styling secondary content.
Reduce visual competition by establishing one dominant task or state, a small number of stable regions, restrained accents, and generous separation while keeping operational meaning explicit.
Treat state as essential content: preserve progress, selection, validation, save or publish status, success feedback, urgency, and recovery even when the surrounding interface is sparse.
Assign expressive elements a job—explain a mental model, motivate progress, identify a content category, or create a focal action—and remove ornament that competes with task comprehension.
Use consistent image treatment, typography, tags, and navigation to turn varied expressive content into a coherent system.
Layer dense work from current health or outcome to trends, exceptions, contributing dimensions, and raw evidence so users can scan first and drill down without losing context.
Separate inputs, assumptions, calculations, outputs, and comparisons visually and semantically; never rely on position or color alone to communicate data role.

Make technical scope persistent by naming project, environment, service, resource, region, version, time range, live state, permission, and secret boundary wherever actions or evidence depend on them.
Use technical density to expose causality and control, not to signal expertise: labels, units, status, exact scope, copyable commands, and safe defaults must remain understandable to a new operator.
Give play a functional role: reduce anxiety, explain a concept, reinforce progress, celebrate a verified result, distinguish identity, or invite the next safe action.
Bind celebration to an inspectable outcome through the completed behavior, achievement condition, earned value, progress count, or next milestone; animation alone must not imply success.
Bind every cinematic hero to decision context through identity, source, metadata, suitability, scope, and a concrete action rather than relying on atmosphere alone.
For consequential or emotional experiences, connect imagery to provenance, measurable state, safeguards, exact commitment, and recovery so emotion cannot substitute for evidence.
Organize the interface around the current object, scope, state, and next operation; use direct labels and stable regions before adding summaries or personality.
At destructive, automated, or costly boundaries, name the affected scope, consequence, run or save state, cost or resource use, history, cancel or stop, and recovery.
Order messages so claims, evidence, tradeoffs, and actions remain distinguishable.
Lead with a recognizable user outcome or completed state before naming the product category, technology, or company ambition.
Make the value concrete by naming the relevant input, task, change, or result closely enough that the intended audience can judge whether it applies.
Follow the outcome immediately with the mechanism that produces it, using process detail, workflow structure, or a legible product state rather than assertion alone.

Name the evidence type and keep it distinct: a product state demonstrates mechanism, a customer result demonstrates an observed outcome, a benchmark demonstrates comparison, an assurance demonstrates control, and a testimonial demonstrates attributed experience.

Make quantitative proof self-describing by attaching the measured outcome to the actor or population, intervention or product use, timeframe, baseline or comparator, unit, and source needed to judge the number.
Preserve uncertainty and transferability limits: identify when evidence comes from one customer, selected examples, commissioned research, a particular dataset, or a specific operating context.

applicability: all supported design reviews and directions
modality_independent_principles: Review hierarchy, comprehension, accessibility, trust, content, and differentiation in the target modality.
Reserve the strongest emphasis for the current state, unresolved consequence, or next meaningful action rather than greetings, tutorials, upgrades, or generic recommendations.
Separate orientation, state, evidence, decision, and secondary exploration through stable regions, spacing, type, order, and contrast instead of relying on one signal alone.
Use consistent form for comparable items and vary size, color, position, or persistence only when the semantic priority or consequence is genuinely different.

Build an explicit semantic definition around important information: name the object, define the measure or status, state scope and time basis, identify source and freshness, and show ownership or authority before users act on it.

Teach workflows as a causal sequence: explain prerequisites, what each stage produces, who participates, expected timing, current progress, remaining work, and what the next transition will make true.
Translate consequential reviews into the underlying people, resources, dates, money, permissions, and obligations, preserving editability and a preview of the exact artifact before commitment.

Keep task context persistent across search, filters, selection, detail, and action: show the active scope, selected count, current object, saved-versus-temporary state, and the result of each operation without forcing users to reconstruct their place.

Prevent form errors with purpose text, appropriate input controls, examples, sensible inherited defaults, conditional fields, and validation close to the source while preserving every valid value and a usable back path.
When an action affects dependent workflow steps, offer explicit downstream choices and explain what will continue, stop, be canceled, be removed, remain preserved, or become inaccessible.

Keep names, labels, instructions, required or optional status, current values, and errors persistently associated with their controls; placeholders and entered content must not become the only way to identify a field.

Make important visual data redundant through direct labels, values, units, legends, symbols, patterns, ranges, written comparisons, and an inspectable table or list alternative so hue, position, or shape is never the sole carrier of meaning.

Use readable type, sufficient contrast, spacing, clear hierarchy, and controls large enough to identify and activate across dense, dark, bright, and data-rich contexts; de-emphasis must not erase essential instructions or status.
Model interactions as explicit transitions with a source state, trigger, target state, timing, prerequisites, and completion condition so users and builders can predict what an action will make true.

Keep interaction context continuous: preserve the affected object, underlying place, current selection, staged changes, and dismissal or return path while menus, popovers, modals, and command surfaces are open.

Separate optimistic acknowledgement from durable completion: show pending or syncing state after immediate feedback, reconcile partial or failed outcomes, and do not let a success notification contradict unresolved work.

Adapt by semantic priority rather than proportional shrinking: preserve current scope, selected object, essential state, primary action, and safe return first, then collapse, move, or defer secondary navigation, inspectors, metadata, and utilities.

Maintain continuity when a multi-pane workspace becomes a compact sequence by preserving selection, title, project or collection, filters, scroll position, unsaved state, and a predictable back path between list and detail.

Test responsive behavior as content and state combinations, including long labels, many panes, wide tables, keyboard visible, empty and error states, selected rows, open menus, active inspectors, and unsaved work—not only at nominal viewport widths.
At the decision boundary, show the exact actor or account, affected object or resource, destination, amount or data scope, permission, and timing needed to verify what will happen.
State consequences in operational terms, including affected dependencies, irreversibility, cost, duration, eligibility, or resulting state, before the final action is available.
Separate current state, observed evidence, inferred risk, and recommended action so a health summary does not become a stronger claim than its visible basis supports.
Place warnings, qualifications, and material terms beside the decision they govern; use linked detail as supporting evidence rather than a substitute for decision-critical disclosure.

Define visual choices by semantic role—surface, text, action, status, focus, border, chart series, heading, body, spacing, and density—then map modes and brands onto those roles instead of exposing unrelated raw values.
Evolve visual systems through explicit save state, legacy mapping, migration notices, and bounded overrides so existing artifacts and behaviors do not silently change.

Define each component through stable anatomy, named properties, bounded variants, and explicit states so optional content and behavior remain understandable without duplicating near-identical components.
Make layered components communicate trigger or parent context, focus scope, dismissal behavior, action priority, and consequence rather than relying on visual elevation alone.
Layer brand expression onto stable semantic roles and interaction contracts so logos, accents, typography, and imagery can vary without changing meaning, priority, or expected behavior.
Specify how user preference, operating-system preference, product defaults, organization policy, and saved personal choices resolve when they disagree.

Create an explicit publication boundary where proposed system changes have a named scope, rationale, owner, review state, version, release note, and effective audience before downstream consumers receive them.
Treat deprecation as a lifecycle with announcement, affected scope, replacement, compatibility period, migration steps, deadline, support path, and final removal rather than a deleted asset.

Adapt by semantic priority: preserve current scope, selected object, consequential state, primary action, and safe return first; collapse, move, summarize, or defer secondary navigation, inspectors, metadata, and utilities.

When simultaneous panes become a compact sequence, preserve selection, title, parent scope, filters, unsaved state, scroll position, and a predictable back path so layout change does not become context loss.
Separate immediate acknowledgement from durable completion, then resolve success into the actual saved, booked, published, or generated product state rather than a disconnected celebratory endpoint.

Make failure and interruption actionable by preserving completed work, identifying the failed scope, explaining what remains uncertain, and offering retry, correction, cancellation, or safe exit without duplicate commitment.

Expose manipulation as a complete contract: identifiable object, available affordance, active tool or mode, valid target or range, live preview, constraint feedback, commit boundary, and recovery path.
Preview outcome continuously while distinguishing transient manipulation from persisted state; make cancel, reset, undo, and redo proportional to consequence and available after commitment.
For batch operations, expose selection count, selection scope, filters, paging implications, affected objects, available actions, and consequence before commitment.
Support expert acceleration as a parallel path over the same semantic actions, permissions, validation, feedback, and undo model used by pointer and assistive interaction.
Bind every time-varying mark to observation, update, forecast, or validity time and distinguish current, predicted, delayed, stale, and unknown states.
Preserve provenance and uncertainty through source, update cadence, units, confidence or forecast status, coverage limits, and non-color cues beside the mapped decision.
Keep asset identity, source, rights, metadata, version, proxy or original status, usage context, and preview available from library through edit, review, render, and publication.
Bind collaboration feedback to an exact version and, where relevant, frame, timecode, layer, region, or object; distinguish discussion, requested change, approval, and resolved status.

Explain why the problem persists through a credible cause—fragmented ownership, manual handoffs, missing visibility, repeated work, uncontrolled risk, or incompatible tools—rather than blaming the user.
Present the solution as a mechanism that changes specific inputs, handoffs, decisions, controls, or outputs; avoid jumping from pain directly to feature inventory or an unearned outcome.

Choose type categories from the job each role must perform—reading, scanning, comparison, action, expression, code, evidence, or annotation—then test whether the resulting voice is true to the brand and credible in its industry context.

Evaluate every proposed family and pairing against role coverage, small-size legibility, similar-character distinction, numerals, punctuation, italics, variable axes, loading, licensing, script support, localization, accessibility, and fallback behavior before treating aesthetic fit as sufficient.
Make every stage independently useful with a descriptive heading, concise claim, mechanism or example, and optional deeper path so scanning and skipping do not destroy comprehension.
Place consequential terms, safeguards, uncertainty, eligibility, fees, and limits before the action they govern, even when doing so interrupts the emotional arc.
Begin with the decision context—who is choosing, the job or outcome, the options in scope, and the few criteria that materially change fit—before presenting a detailed comparison.
Explain recommendations and defaults through explicit audience, assumptions, evidence, and tradeoffs; preserve a neutral path to inspect and select every viable option.
Reveal information according to the current task, user intent, decision consequence, and need for inspection; do not equate infrequent, advanced, or complex content with safe-to-hide content.

Keep price, renewal, eligibility, risk, irreversible effects, permissions, destructive consequences, and other material terms visible before the decision they govern, regardless of the disclosure pattern.

Explain what each personalization input changes, where it applies, how long it persists, and whether it was explicitly supplied, inferred from behavior, inherited from policy, or derived from current context.
Give users correction at the level of the signal and outcome—item, topic, source, goal, role, default, inferred fact, or remembered detail—and state what future behavior the correction will affect.

Give every field, value, state, message, and action a persistent semantic label that names the concept or operation; use supporting text for format, units, scope, evidence, consequence, or examples rather than repeating the label.

Make validation and errors local, specific, and recovery-oriented: identify the affected field or object, unmet rule or known cause, retained work, resulting state, and safest next action without blaming the user.
Tie expressive choices to the product mechanism, audience, or artifacts users create; pair metaphor and category cues with concrete examples, evidence, constraints, and a clear action.
Evaluate differentiation against comprehension, task success, accessibility, performance, localization, trust, maintenance, and recognizable value—not aesthetic novelty or competitor distance alone.

Choose palette character—warm or cool, muted or saturated, monochrome or multicolor, light or dark—from brand voice, content, environment, task duration, and industry credibility; do not reduce industries to fixed color stereotypes.

Use semantic color proportionally to consequence and always pair status, severity, gain, loss, risk, success, warning, and error with text, iconography, shape, position, or pattern that preserves meaning without color.
Name the specific uncertainty or risk at the decision point, then show the relevant safeguard, evidence, remaining limitation, accountable party, and next step rather than using generic reassurance.

Describe reversibility precisely: what can be cancelled, refunded, restored, revoked, archived, downgraded, exported, or deleted; who can do it; through which path; within what time; at what cost; and what state or data remains.

Define canonical names for objects, actors, scopes, states, and operations; use one term for one concept and introduce a different term only when lifecycle, authority, or user meaning genuinely differs.
Let tone adapt to context while keeping state, cause, evidence, consequence, retained work, and recovery literal; do not use warmth, humor, confidence, or apology to blur operational truth.

Name accessibility settings by the interface behavior they change—text size, contrast, motion, sound, captions, timing, focus, input, or navigation—without diagnosing, stigmatizing, or requiring users to justify the preference.

Offer accommodations and human assistance through ordinary, respectful language that describes the available path, expected effort, timing, privacy, and outcome without requiring disclosure of disability or presenting support as an exception.

Model language, region, market, currency, units, time zone, calendar, and content availability as separate preferences or states whenever they can produce different behavior; show the source, scope, precedence, and effect of each.

Treat culturally dependent icons, colors, metaphors, examples, address conventions, consent language, and legal claims as reviewable content rather than universal meaning; retain a plain semantic label and jurisdiction-aware validation.

Define the evaluation contract before reviewing: artifact and revision, audience, task scenario, environment, constraints, success conditions, heuristic or requirement set, evidence sources, exclusions, and decision owner.

Close the loop by recording disposition, owner, target revision, implemented change, retest method, verification evidence, residual risk, regressions checked, and final decision; approval binds only the exact reviewed revision.
Keep the active organization, workspace, environment, legal entity, resource, and affected population persistently visible; distinguish navigation context from the scope where a change will apply.

Preview high-impact and bulk changes as a concrete diff: selected targets, included and excluded objects, before and after state, dependencies, downstream effects, notification behavior, reversibility, retained data, and recovery procedure.

Separate source severity, operational priority, confidence, exposure, business consequence, lifecycle state, and response urgency; show the evidence and rubric behind each rather than relying on color or one composite risk score.

Maintain an immutable, queryable operational record connecting actor and authority, evidence, hypothesis, decision, action, target, before and after state, time, source, outcome, communication, recovery, and later correction; bind resolution to verification rather than status alone.

Keep source and runtime lineage continuous: repository, branch or tag, immutable revision, author and review state, configuration fingerprint, build or artifact identity, target environment, deployment, active version, and rollback ancestor.

Preview consequential developer actions with exact source and target, environment, configuration diff, affected services and dependencies, credentials or data touched, expected downtime or behavior, authorization, verification, partial failure, rollback, and audit record.

Translate the user's request into an inspectable execution contract: intended outcome, target objects and people, scope, constraints, assumptions, inputs, allowed tools and actions, expected artifacts, approval points, stop conditions, and verifiable completion criteria.

Declare completion only from verified external state: identify attempted and successful actions, changed and unchanged targets, partial failures, pending work, notifications, artifacts, evidence, cost, residual risk, and rollback or correction path; retain an immutable task and tool history.

Treat every behavioral principle as a context-bound hypothesis, not a universal law: name the user, task, environment, cognitive constraint, predicted effect, possible counter-effect, affected groups, and evidence needed to accept or reject it.

Preserve autonomy with a visible neutral alternative, informed consequence, proportional friction, granular consent, correction, exit, undo, and recovery; make the easiest path compatible with the user's interests rather than only the organization's preferred outcome.
Place current state, target state, billing or timing consequence, affected scope, and the exact commitment in one reviewable decision frame.

Scale confirmation friction to consequence: ordinary plan selection needs clear review, while irreversible deletion may require identity verification or a target-specific phrase without obscuring a visible cancel path.

Present each material choice with its purpose, included and excluded outcomes, risk, cost, timing, affected scope, and correction path before the user commits; never defer a decision-changing fact to a later step.

Make accept, refuse, defer, revise, and withdraw recognizable and comparably understandable; do not change prominence, effort, defaults, order, or information flow to manufacture the preferred answer.
Connect each reminder to a user-recognizable goal, task, threshold, or changed state, and expose skip, dismiss, snooze, pause, reschedule, or disable in proportion to the interruption.
Keep target, activity, progress, elapsed time, remaining work, streak, reward, and outcome as separate states so attention metrics do not impersonate meaningful achievement.

Organize learning around meaningful product outcomes and real objects, not a tour of interface regions; distinguish required setup, recommended improvement, optional education, and work pending on another actor.

Teach a capability at the moment it becomes relevant using one bounded concept, a representative example or demonstration, its constraints or access state, and choices to try, learn more, defer, dismiss, or finish.

Reduce extraneous load before simplifying the task itself: remove unrelated content, group information by the decision or action it supports, use familiar structure and language, and keep necessary instructions adjacent to the step where they apply.

Externalize memory through visible current state, prior choices, completed and remaining steps, examples, defaults, saved work, and review surfaces; never require recall when the interface can provide recognition or continuity.

Before designing a behavioral intervention, state the user outcome, behavioral mechanism, organizational incentive, expected benefit, plausible harm, affected groups, counter-hypothesis, and stop condition; an uplift target alone is not an ethical rationale.

Measure user welfare alongside business outcomes through comprehension, voluntary refusal, correction, delayed regret, complaint, trust, task value, distributional effects, and durable control; conversion, engagement, completion, or consent rate cannot establish benefit by themselves.

Keep the affected object, user input, workflow position, prior successful state, and surrounding task visible or restorable while explaining what failed and what remains safe, pending, changed, or unknown.

Route help from the current object and task into relevant guidance first, then searchable documentation, examples, peer support, feedback, and human support without replacing the workspace or losing the return path.

Separate consent by specific purpose, data category, recipient, duration, and consequence; distinguish required processing from optional personalization, advertising, improvement, sharing, and support access.

Make consent durable and revisitable through visible current state, later settings, withdrawal, export, deletion, saved confirmation, and any processing or data that necessarily remains after a request.

Make ongoing value inspectable through the user's own durable state: current plan or program, saved work, progress, usage, benefits already received, next meaningful action, and the future state that continuation enables; do not substitute generic promotion for earned continuity.

Treat return and resumption as restoration rather than restart: preserve object identity, prior choices, completion state, next step, remaining effort, paused or expired status, and a low-friction route back into meaningful work.

Separate account identity, sign-in method, verification factor, recovery channel, trusted device, active session, and connected provider as distinct states; show which are configured, verified, current, weaker, unavailable, or incomplete.

Design recovery as a visible assurance sequence: identify the account without oversharing, show the masked verification destination, allow alternate or support routes, disclose material side effects, confirm credential change, and state what the person should do next.

Before transfer, identify the source, destination, data objects, selected scope, format, account, access permission, transformation, overwrite or duplication behavior, limits, and whether the operation copies, moves, continuously synchronizes, or deletes anything.

Close the loop with a verifiable result that separates created, updated, skipped, duplicated, associated, missing, and failed items; provide error evidence, correction or rollback options, retained-source state, and a direct route to inspect the destination.

Keep selection scope continuously visible through exact count, selected-versus-all distinction, active filters, excluded or ineligible items, destination or cohort, and a clear way to inspect, adjust, or clear the selection before action.

Close every bulk action with result accounting that separates requested, changed, unchanged, skipped, ineligible, failed, moved, archived, or deleted items and preserves actor, time, destination, undo or recovery, and an inspectable history.

Choose the history model before choosing the layout: collaborative activity should optimize orientation and follow-up, administrative audit logs should optimize exact evidence and filtering, and object version history should optimize comparison and recovery.

Keep history connected to present context through stable object identity, deep links, previews, current-state labels, and explicit before-and-after or selected-revision comparison; never imply that an event log is itself the current state.
Model notification state separately from work state: unread, read, seen, dismissed, archived, snoozed, assigned, resolved, and completed must not collapse into one badge or clearing action.

Make every notification answer why the person received it, who or what caused it, what object and workspace it concerns, what changed, when it happened, whether action is required, and where to inspect or act.

Treat attention as a user cost: choose interruption level from consequence, required response window, current task, reversibility, and the cost of missing the event, never from the sender's desire for engagement.

Use the least disruptive channel that still makes the state perceivable: prefer contextual status near the affected work, then persistent banners or inboxes, reserving focus-taking alerts and modal interruption for rare events requiring immediate action.

Keep the search contract visible: identify scope, searchable object types, query, active filters, sort, result count, freshness or source limits, and whether matching is exact, semantic, personalized, or permission-bounded.

Make each result provide enough information scent to predict the destination through title, type, source, hierarchy, matched context, relevant attributes, state, date, provenance, and available action without opening every item.

Support both known-item lookup and exploratory foraging: preserve a simple direct query path while offering visible scopes, categories, facets, related concepts, and alternate routes for people who cannot name the destination precisely.

Externalize the evolving query model through retained terms, result counts, applied-filter overviews, facet values, sort, scope, and individual or global removal; do not require people to remember why the set changed.

Keep progress truthful and recoverable through stable section names, current and completed state, save status, safe back navigation, resumable drafts, retained answers, and an honest distinction between section completion, validation, review, submission, and downstream acceptance.

Before consequential submission, provide a complete, scannable review grouped by the original sections, mark missing or skipped answers, offer precise edit routes that return to review, and label the final action by its actual commitment.

Prevent errors before messaging them: ask only necessary questions, use familiar and semantically appropriate controls, state constraints before entry, accept reasonable formats, preserve prior answers, and avoid requiring redundant recall.

For consequential submission, make the commitment checked, confirmed, or reversible: present a complete review, targeted change routes, retained answers, an action-specific submit label, and proportional confirmation or undo.

Begin with an explicit analytical contract: state the question, decision or hypothesis, population or object scope, measure definition, dimensions, time and timezone basis, comparison or baseline, denominator, source, freshness, exclusions, and whether the work is exploratory, monitoring, or confirmatory.

Keep interpretation proportional to evidence by exposing numerator and denominator, absolute and relative values, baseline, sample or coverage, missing and suppressed data, uncertainty or estimation, source changes, freshness, and noncomparable periods; distinguish observed pattern, generated summary, hypothesis, and validated conclusion.

Make every quantitative claim self-describing through the question or intended decision, population or object scope, measure definition, numerator and denominator, unit, time and timezone basis, comparison or baseline, source, freshness, exclusions, and whether the result is observed, estimated, modeled, or forecast.

Expose uncertainty and data quality when they can change interpretation through sample or coverage, missing and suppressed values, estimation method, range and coverage basis, rounding, revision, source change, and limitations; explain uncertainty in plain language and withhold or qualify comparisons that the evidence cannot support.

Create a durable case from the person's actual task context: preserve the affected account, order, resource, transaction, or workflow; capture what happened, impact and urgency, timing, attempted fixes, desired outcome, attachments, safe diagnostics, language or accessibility needs, and contact preference without demanding information the service already holds.

Treat resolution as a verifiable outcome rather than an agent declaration: state the finding and reasons, action or remedy, affected scope, owner, timing, dependencies, evidence of completion, remaining limitations, and how the person can confirm, correct, reject, reopen, appeal, or escalate with the full history retained; request feedback only after the outcome is clear and never as a condition of remedy.

Give the affected person meaningful voice before deciding: make the route easy to find and use, support suitable channels and representation, let them describe what happened, impact, evidence, access needs, and sought outcome in their own terms, acknowledge every material issue, and provide a fair opportunity to correct the record or respond to adverse information.

Make recovery proportional to the actual harm and verify it: stop continuing harm, restore the person as nearly as practical, correct records or access, refund or compensate where appropriate, acknowledge and apologize without deflection, explain prevention work, confirm completion with evidence, preserve reopening, and measure both fair process and durable outcome rather than deflection or closure alone.

applicability: message correction, forwarding, retention, and export
modality_independent_principles: Establish a visible conversation envelope before sending: identify destination, topic or object, purpose, participants and roles, direct addressees versus observers, workspace or tenant, privacy and external-participant status, retention boundary, and notification reach; keep that envelope visible beside the draft and require fresh review when audience or destination changes.

Promote consequential outcomes out of conversational implication into durable objects: record decisions, approvals, requests, promises, action items, owners, due dates, affected scope, status, evidence, and supersession with a backlink to the exact message context; do not treat a reaction, read receipt, silence, generated summary, or informal acknowledgment as agreement or completion.

Design for a purpose-relative grounding criterion: before participants act, make the current topic, referenced objects, relevant prior turns, known facts, assumptions, unresolved ambiguity, participant and system capabilities, and evidence of understanding visible enough for the consequence; increase explicit restatement and verification as ambiguity, delay, audience size, automation, or harm rises.

Distinguish receipt, attention, comprehension, acknowledgment, agreement, authorization, commitment, and completion: use lightweight acknowledgment for low-risk continuity, targeted confirmation for material parameters, and explicit scope, actor, action, consequence, and durable evidence for consequential decisions; never infer commitment from presence, read state, reaction, silence, or conversational fluency.

applicability: order, payment, delivery, and synchronization exceptions
modality_independent_principles: Create a shared situation view organized around what is known, inferred, unknown, changing, and next: show severity and priority rationale, affected and potentially affected scope, user or business impact, dependencies, current operating state, timeline, hypotheses with evidence, recent actions and outcomes, ownership, command roles, open questions, next checkpoint, and data freshness.

Treat recovery and learning as evidence-bearing phases: distinguish contained, mitigated, restored, monitored, resolved, closed, and recurrent; require service or process health, affected-record reconciliation, user-impact review, residual risk, and observation-window evidence before closure, then preserve a blameless chronology, contributing conditions, detection and response gaps, decisions, communication, follow-up owners and due dates, and verification that improvements took effect.

applicability: service, logistics, finance, and workforce operations
modality_independent_principles: Support all three situation-awareness horizons: help operators perceive relevant state and change through source, time, freshness, threshold and missingness; comprehend meaning through scope, dependency, consequence, confidence and operating mode; and project plausible evolution through trend, rate, capacity, propagation, deadlines, forecast assumptions, and explicit uncertainty.

Design response as a learning control loop: coordinate explicit command, operations, communication, planning and specialist roles; verify containment, restoration and residual risk against objectives and affected users; preserve a blameless evidence timeline; and convert detection, mitigation, coordination and communication lessons into owned changes whose effectiveness is later measured.

Bind every request to an exact review object: show a stable request ID, requester, purpose, artifact or resource, version or hash, affected scope, material changes, requested decision, evidence and checks, policy or criteria, urgency, desired effective time, and expiry; any material edit creates a linked revision and invalidates prior approval rather than moving the approval to the latest version.

Record a decision as durable evidence: preserve decision maker, role and authority, exact object and version, outcome, reasons, evidence considered, conditions, scope, effective and expiry time, dependencies, timestamp, and attestation; never promote a comment, reaction, view, silence, reviewer count, or generated summary into approval.

Begin with the control objective and map incompatible duties across request, create, modify, review, approve, execute, reconcile, administer, and audit: assign roles and system permissions so one actor cannot both cause and conceal a material error, abuse, or unauthorized change; document exceptions and compensating controls when staffing makes full separation impractical.

Bind authorization to what was actually reviewed: present all significant object, scope, consequence, version, and transaction data; require an outcome-specific act with clear meaning; invalidate authorization after any material change; limit validity by time and state; and verify the same approved object and conditions again before execution.

Make rule logic readable at both policy and case level: use explicit all, any, none, threshold, sequence, fallback, default, and missing or indeterminate semantics; expose grouping and precedence without relying on indentation alone; provide plain-language and structured views that remain equivalent; and for a selected subject and resource, show which facts were used, which rules matched or failed, how conflicts combined, and why the final outcome and obligations resulted.

Treat exceptions as governed subordinate records rather than hidden edits or permanent bypasses: identify governing rule, affected subject, resource, action and environment, requestor, need and evidence, risk and impacted parties, reviewer authority and conflict, compensating controls, narrower scope, effective and expiry time, review and revocation triggers, usage and incidents, outcome and reasons, and whether recurring exceptions require the base policy to be corrected.

Make precedence and conflict deterministically legible: expose hierarchy, specificity, inheritance, order, overrides, deny or permit priority, one-applicable requirements, incompatible obligations, circularity and unreachable rules; show the same representative case through each applicable rule and the combination path; treat no match, missing attributes, error, indeterminate, deny, permit, conditional outcome, and not applicable as distinct states.

Govern exceptions and corrective action as evidence-bearing feedback: require a narrow case, reason, risk, reviewer authority and independence, compensating controls, effective and expiry time, monitoring, revocation, affected parties, decision and appeal; distinguish exception from rule change and enforcement failure; aggregate exception use, inconsistent outcomes, overrides, incidents and complaints to find root causes, repair deficient policy, verify remediation, and preserve prior decisions without normalizing permanent bypass.

Model context as an inspectable inventory of distinct state: current prompt and session, conversation history, saved facts, preferences and custom instructions, inferred attributes, project or task context, uploaded files, connected sources, workspace knowledge, organization policy, feedback, analytics, safety records, and model-improvement data; show which are temporary, retained, searchable, reusable, shared, exported, or used to adapt future behavior instead of collapsing them into one memory label.

Give every context item provenance and scope: identify exact content or concise representation, subject, author or inference origin, source object and version, collection time, freshness, confidence where inferred, purpose, permitted operations, active account, identity, project, task, agent, workspace and organization, eligible audiences, geographic or policy boundary, retention and expiry, and whether it influences retrieval, response generation, ranking, automation, personalization, analytics, safety review, or model improvement.

applicability: data rights retention deletion and portability
modality_independent_principles: Evaluate every information flow in its actual context: identify the data subject, sender or source, recipient and downstream actors, information type and sensitivity, purpose, expected benefit, authority, collection or inference method, transmission and reuse rules, social or professional norms, power relationship, geography, retention and consequence; treat movement between personal, workplace, health, financial, educational, family and public contexts as a new decision even when one organization controls both.

Provide meaningful data agency without transferring all privacy labor to individuals: make actors, data, purpose, source, inference, scope, audience, persistence, consequences and defaults understandable at the relevant moment; support access, item-level correction, completion, restriction, objection, withdrawal, deletion, export and portability through usable controls; preserve a protected service path after optional refusal and use organizational safeguards when granular choice cannot make an inappropriate flow acceptable.

applicability: AI prompt model and agent experiments
modality_independent_principles: Make the experiment a versioned decision contract: preserve the decision question, falsifiable hypothesis, rationale and prior evidence, accountable owner and reviewers, exact control and treatment artifacts, unit and method of assignment, eligibility and exclusions, traffic allocation, exposure event, primary outcome, guardrails, segments, minimum meaningful effect, analysis model, power or precision target, planned duration, stopping rules, risk controls, rollback path and decision policy; material changes create a linked revision rather than rewriting the running test.

Present evidence as a decision input rather than a winner badge: show metric definition, direction, numerator and denominator, absolute and relative effects, uncertainty, sample and exposure counts, time window, data freshness, guardrail outcomes, planned and exploratory analyses, subgroup coverage, novelty and carryover risk, quality diagnostics and practical significance; distinguish no evidence, insufficient evidence, evidence of no material effect and evidence of harm.

applicability: AI model prompt and agent evaluations
modality_independent_principles: Test whether the design can answer the stated decision question before exposing anyone: require a falsifiable hypothesis, appropriate control, unit and method of assignment, representative eligibility, stable measurement, exact treatment versions, primary outcome and guardrails, minimum meaningful effect, power or precision rationale, planned duration and analysis, interference and carryover assessment, and a decision policy that permits no-change or inconclusive outcomes.

Communicate evidence without binary significance theater: show estimand, population, metric formula, numerator and denominator, base rates, absolute and relative effects, interval estimates, sample and exposure counts, practical importance, uncertainty and assumptions; distinguish planned from exploratory analyses and no evidence from evidence of no meaningful effect; correct for multiplicity and avoid selecting only favorable metrics, windows or segments.

Make every available alternative discoverable before commitment and controllable during use: identify captions, subtitle and spoken languages, narrated visual alternatives, complete multimodal transcripts, sign interpretation, chapters and text equivalents; distinguish human-reviewed, generated, translated, live, delayed, partial and unavailable states; disclose material limits without making people start playback or reveal a disability to learn what is offered.

Provide an equivalent route to the essential outcome, not merely an attached text dump: carry instructions, decisions, actions, alerts, assessments, links and important visual or auditory context into the appropriate alternative; keep interactive options operable; and test whether a person can understand and complete the task through the chosen combination of modalities.

Define equivalence by access to essential information, context, interaction and outcome rather than identical presentation: identify what speech, meaningful sound, action, expression, visual change, on-screen text, timing and interactivity contribute; provide captions, description, descriptive transcripts, sign language or structural alternatives as the audience requires; and preserve language, sequence, semantics and actionable controls.

Protect privacy and dignity around access preferences and captured communication: do not require a person to reveal diagnosis to obtain alternatives; distinguish personal preferences from shared-device defaults; give notice and meaningful control over live transcription, recording, retention, access, correction and deletion; avoid treating one modality as the normal experience and alternatives as burdensome exceptions.

Define and expose distinct durability states around the exact object or action: unsaved in memory, saved locally, prepared for offline use, queued for transmission, sending, accepted remotely, synchronized across relevant devices, completed by the business process, failed, conflicted or cancelled; use plain language, timestamps and affected scope so a positive local-save signal is never mistaken for remote acceptance or final completion.

Resolve divergence without silent overwrite: identify the exact fields, blocks, files or actions in conflict; preserve both versions and authorship; compare meaningful differences in context; auto-merge only demonstrably compatible changes; let authorized people keep, combine, duplicate or defer; preview consequences; and retain reversible history with a clear resulting canonical version.

applicability: data ownership, export and long-term access
modality_independent_principles: Model continuity as an explicit state machine rather than a connectivity icon: distinguish local persistence, queued intent, attempted transmission, remote receipt, durable acceptance, downstream processing, convergence and final outcome; bind each state to the exact object, revision and action; expose timestamps, provenance and uncertainty; and never use success language for a stage whose later guarantees have not been met.

Preserve user intent before optimizing convergence: make local work durable and inspectable, retain stable action identity and ordering, preserve drafts and both sides of divergence, support export and recovery independent of service availability, and avoid resolution strategies that silently discard semantically distinct work merely because one timestamp or server is newer.

Turn recognition into inspectable and editable intent before commitment: show partial and final text where a display exists, preserve language and relevant context, mark uncertain spans without overstating confidence, allow touch, keyboard or speech correction at the word, parameter or whole-request level, retain the original draft until replacement is confirmed, and never make a transcript the sole record when the original audio carries essential meaning.

Scale confirmation to consequence and reversibility: use lightweight grounding for ordinary search, explicit review for names, addresses, medication, recipients and shared messages, and exact confirmation before payment, consent, deletion, publication or physical control; state what was understood and what will happen; distinguish a recognized utterance from authorized action and a requested action from completed outcome.

applicability: smart home, vehicle and physical control
shared devices, kiosks and ambient systems
children, atypical speech and multilingual use
modality_independent_principles: Preserve the distinction between signal, words, meaning, intent, authorization and outcome: expose what the system captured and inferred at the useful grain; represent uncertainty without claiming that a score proves correctness; ground ordinary parameters lightly; explicitly confirm consequential parameters and actions; and never let recognition alone authorize irreversible, financial, legal, health, safety or physical-world effects.

Design repair as a first-class cooperative path: expect hesitation, self-correction, code-switching, noise, interruption, no input, no match and system failure; preserve valid context; support one-step spoken or nonspoken correction, repeat, undo and review; explain the specific recoverable problem without blaming speech; bound reprompts; and offer an equivalent route or graceful exit before frustration becomes exclusion.

applicability: barcodes, QR codes and visual search
modality_independent_principles: Separate capture, recognition, extraction, authenticity, ownership, eligibility and final outcome: show recognized code, document type, fields or amount before using them; bind extracted values to their source region; flag uncertainty and mismatch; require exact review for names, identifiers, dates, medication, account and monetary values; and never imply that a clear image, OCR result, liveness result or successful upload independently proves a later claim.

Scale commitment and recovery to consequence: preview the exact pages, fields, recipient, account and action before legal, financial, health, identity or public submission; keep recapture and precise edit routes; distinguish saved draft, uploaded, received, under review, accepted and rejected; preserve a receipt and source-bound correction path; and offer trained human or offline review when automated capture repeatedly fails.

applicability: barcodes, QR codes and visual lookup
modality_independent_principles: Treat acquisition, transformation, recognition and decision as separate accountable stages: preserve source identity and capture conditions; record crop, enhancement, compression, redaction and extraction; bind every recognized value to its source region and version; distinguish image quality, OCR confidence, document authenticity, person-to-evidence binding, eligibility and final action; and expose the evidence needed to review each claim.

Require consequence-sensitive review and completion evidence: before financial, legal, health, identity, safety or public action, present exact source pages, extracted values, destination, recipient and commitment; distinguish captured, saved, uploaded, received, validated, under review, accepted and rejected; preserve receipts and correction routes; and ensure a successful technical transfer never masquerades as substantive approval.

applicability: editorial feeds, discovery and media libraries
profiles, people, places and identity context
responsive cards, overlays, loading and fallback states
brand illustration and cross-theme art direction
modality_independent_principles: Assign every image one explicit interface role before selecting its style: identity, object preview, evidence, instruction, status, editorial content, atmosphere or decoration; define the claim it may support, the adjacent information that must carry meaning without it and whether it is interactive; and do not let one attractive asset ambiguously stand in for product state, proof, action and brand at once.

Treat functional and evidentiary imagery as inspectable information: show source, owner or subject, time or freshness, representative-versus-illustrative status, edits or transformations and confidence or verification only when supported; provide detail viewing when crop can hide material facts; never use idealized stock, generated, edited or example imagery as evidence of a real person, product, place, result or security state.

applicability: people, profiles, avatars and identity context
responsive cards, crops, overlays and themes
provenance, consent, privacy and content governance
modality_independent_principles: Classify an image by purpose in its exact context before styling or describing it: decorative imagery contributes no required information and should be suppressible; informative imagery needs an equivalent for its relevant meaning; functional imagery needs an action or destination name; complex imagery needs an adequate extended representation; identity and evidence imagery need context, provenance and higher scrutiny; and the same asset may require a different classification when its use changes.

Separate what an image depicts from what its history can support: label representative, illustrative, edited, composite, generated and documentary uses where confusion is material; preserve available creator, source, time and modification provenance; make inspection proportionate to consequence; treat credentials and signatures as evidence about origin and change rather than proof that the depicted claim is true; and communicate absent or broken provenance without declaring the content false.

applicability: documents, images, audio, video and structured data
mobile capture, system pickers and drag-and-drop
sharing, versioning, replacement, download and removal
modality_independent_principles: Frame the file request before presenting a picker: name the purpose, destination or affected record, whether submission is required, who can access the result, acceptable alternatives, supported types, count and size limits, expected processing and retention; ask for a file only when its information is necessary; and avoid a generic attachment icon when the person must infer what evidence, format or disclosure is expected.

Keep uploaded content anchored to ownership and access context: show the containing record, workspace, conversation, audience or recipient; distinguish private draft, shared, published and externally accessible states; preserve uploader, source, time, version and processing provenance when relevant; warn before a file crosses an access boundary; and do not infer that an attachment inherits safe visibility merely because the surrounding screen is familiar.

applicability: imports, training sources and automated processing
modality_independent_principles: Justify the submission at the field and purpose level: ask only for information necessary to deliver the stated outcome, explain why a file is needed and whether another path can satisfy the requirement, avoid collecting whole documents when a smaller attestation or field is adequate, accept interoperable formats where feasible, and periodically review whether the content, metadata and retained copies remain relevant and necessary.

Communicate lifecycle state as verifiable facts: distinguish queued, transferred, server-received, validating, scanning, processing, accepted, ready, rejected, quarantined, failed, withdrawn and deleted; announce progress and results programmatically without stealing focus; identify partial success per item; never use a single success mark to imply that content is safe, processed, shared or durably retained; and attach retry, correction and support to the state that actually failed.

applicability: products, services, providers, places and digital content
public reviews and private operational feedback
provider responses, complaints and service recovery
reputation affecting ranking, access, work or income
modality_independent_principles: Present aggregates as bounded evidence rather than a trust badge: show the review count and relevant population, distribution, recency, version or transaction context and category breakdown; distinguish verified interaction, incentivized, imported, translated or summarized content; avoid excessive precision and unexplained weighting; and do not let a high average hide a tiny sample, polarized distribution, stale history or materially changed offering.

Govern downstream reputation effects as consequential decisions: document how ratings influence search, badges, prices, eligibility, visibility, deactivation, work or income; use sufficient and comparable evidence, freshness and confidence; detect manipulation and coordinated abuse; limit the effect of isolated or biased ratings; provide notice, explanation, correction and human appeal before serious penalties; and audit outcomes across reviewer and subject groups rather than optimizing only review volume or average score.

applicability: product, provider, place and content ratings
public reviews and private quality signals
moderation, response, correction, dispute and appeal
modality_independent_principles: Treat solicitation as a source of measurement bias: document who is asked, when, how often, after which outcomes and through which channel; make decline and later response possible; avoid prompting only satisfied people, gating criticism, conditioning incentives on sentiment or interrupting people before meaningful use; compare respondents with the eligible population; and interpret increased review volume as changed sampling until evidence shows otherwise.

Apply procedural safeguards when reputation becomes an allocation mechanism: identify every use in ranking, badges, pricing, access, matching, deactivation or work distribution; evaluate comparability, bias, manipulation, sample sufficiency and temporal relevance; limit the effect of anomalous feedback; provide notice and an intelligible explanation; allow evidence correction and contextual response; require proportionate human review before serious loss; and audit error and outcome disparities for both reviewers and reviewed people.

applicability: real-time availability, requests and temporary holds
confirmation, preparation, changes, cancellation and refunds
modality_independent_principles: Represent availability as a scoped and time-sensitive fact: show the search criteria and freshness, distinguish available, limited, unavailable, tentative, requestable, held and sold states, explain material eligibility or dependency checks, offer nearby dates, times, locations, providers or equivalent resources, and avoid implying that viewing or selecting a slot guarantees inventory until the system has actually reserved it.

Test the lifecycle as an allocation system: verify keyboard, screen-reader, voice and touch access to calendars and slots; time zones, daylight-saving changes and overnight spans; simultaneous demand, stale inventory, duplicate actions, hold expiry, partial payment and reconnect; accessible-resource guarantees; waitlist ordering, offer expiry and digital exclusion; provider changes, overbooking and no-shows; and audit who receives which inventory, price, priority and recovery rather than measuring conversion alone.

applicability: events, tickets, classes and shared facilities
limited inventory, providers and time slots
temporary holds, requests, waitlists and standby
pricing, deposits, cancellation and no-show rules
provider disruption, overbooking, substitution and refunds
modality_independent_principles: Select an allocation rule deliberately rather than defaulting to fastest-click wins: evaluate first-come, priority, lottery, batch, queue, invitation and provider-discretion models against demand, harm, urgency, gaming, bot access, connectivity, disability, work schedule and digital literacy; publish the rule and material exceptions; use identity or eligibility controls proportionately; and audit whether intermediaries, automation or privileged groups capture scarce capacity.

Allocate disruption risk explicitly and provide proportionate recovery: distinguish user cancellation, missed attendance, provider cancellation, overbooking and significant change; notify through chosen accessible channels; show original and changed commitments; offer suitable alternatives without preselecting away a refund or release option; preserve exact accessibility and dependency needs; restore capacity and waitlist opportunity consistently; and do not shift provider-caused failure into opaque credit, penalty or repeated user effort.

applicability: services, travel, food and digital purchases
repair, replacement, exchange, refund and credit
mail, carrier, pickup and store-return logistics
card, wallet, installment, gift and mixed payments
consumer, seller, carrier, lender and platform coordination
modality_independent_principles: Calculate value restoration transparently: show item amount, quantity, discounts, promotions, tax, original and return shipping, service or restocking charges, used benefits, partial fulfillment, prior credits and remaining installment balance; identify the exact refund destination and expected amount and timing; distinguish estimated from final value pending inspection; explain rounding and allocation across mixed tenders; and never describe store credit as equivalent to cash without explicit choice.

Make rejection, partial outcomes and appeal specific and repairable: identify the item, evidence, policy version, condition finding, amount and responsible decision-maker; show what was accepted and what remains disputed; provide a bounded correction, additional-evidence, seller response, platform review or payment-dispute path as appropriate; pause avoidable collections on genuinely disputed value; preserve communications and custody evidence; and never close the only support route because an automated or first-line decision rejected the claim.

applicability: card, wallet, installment and mixed payment
evidence, inspection, logistics, denial and appeal
modality_independent_principles: Assign burden according to cause and control: distinguish changed mind, customer damage, defect, misdescription, non-delivery, provider cancellation, delay and platform or payment error; place shipping, evidence, fees, repeated contact and timing risk on the party best able to prevent or verify the failure; reduce proof when the business already holds tracking or operational evidence; do not charge people to correct business-caused failure; and explain any retained amount as a proportionate, itemized consequence rather than a generic penalty.

Restore the correct form and amount of value: begin from the original transaction allocation, include required item value, quantity, tax, delivery and mandatory charges, account for discounts, benefits, partial fulfillment and mixed tenders, return value through the original payment path unless the person knowingly chooses a lawful alternative, coordinate merchant and lender balances, pause avoidable collection of genuinely disputed amounts, and never substitute expiring or restricted credit for money without explicit informed choice.
